title: Reel Music
content:
The Beatles’ albums in order – complete list! » Reel Music

Recorded: 1964-1970
Producers: George Martin, Phil Spector

Released: 22 March 1982 (US), 23 March 1982 (UK)

Personnel

John Lennon: vocals, electric guitar, acoustic guitar, electric piano, harpsichord, banjo, harmonica, percussion
Paul McCartney: vocals, bass guitar, electric guitar, piano, double bass, tambourine, maracas
George Harrison: vocals, electric guitar, acoustic guitar, violin, claves, tambourine, percussion
Ringo Starr: vocals, drums, congas, cowbell, tambourine, percussion
George Martin: piano, vocals
Billy Preston: organ, electric piano
Mal Evans: vocals, bass drum
Neil Aspinall: vocals, percussion
Norman Smith: bongos, hi-hat
Johnnie Scott: tenor flute, alto flute
Sidney Sax, Patrick Halling, Eric Bowie, John Ronayne, Jack Rothstein, Ralph Elman, Andrew McGee, Jack Greene, Louis Stevens, John Jezzard, Jack Richards: violin
Lionel Ross, Eldon Fox, Bram Martin, Terry Weil, Lionel Ross, Jack Holmes: cello
Rex Morris, Don Honeywill: tenor saxophone
David Mason, Elgar Howarth, Roy Copestake, John Wilbraham, Stanley Woods: trumpet
Neil Sanders, Tony Tunstall, Morris Miller: horn
Evan Watkins, Harry Spain: trombone
Gordon Lewin: clarinet
Jack Emblow: accordion
Linda McCartney, Pattie Harrison, Jane Asher, Geoff Emerick, Mick Jagger, Keith Richards, Marianne Faithfull, Mike McCartney, Eric Clapton, Brian Jones, Marianne Faithfull, Alf Bicknell, Graham Nash, Keith Moon, Hunter Davies, Gary Leeds, Peggie Allen, Wendy Horan, Pat Whitmore, Jill Utting, June Day, Sylvia King, Irene King, G Mallen, Fred Lucas, Mike Redway, John O’Neill, F Dachtler, Allan Grant, D Griffiths, J Smith, J Fraser: vocals

Tracklisting

‘A Hard Day’s Night’
‘I Should Have Known Better’
‘Can’t Buy Me Love’
‘And I Love Her’
‘Help!’
‘You’ve Got To Hide Your Love Away’
‘Ticket To Ride’
‘Magical Mystery Tour’
‘I Am The Walrus’
‘Yellow Submarine’
‘All You Need Is Love’
‘Let It Be’
‘Get Back’
‘The Long And Winding Road’

The Beatles compilation album Reel Music was released in March 1982.

The 14-song double album brought together songs from the band’s five films: A Hard Day’s Night (1964), Help! (1965), Magical Mystery Tour (1967), Yellow Submarine (1968), and Let It Be (1970).

Released to coincide with a theatrical re-release of A Hard Day’s Night, the album contained several rare mixes. It was the first time the UK stereo mixes of ‘A Hard Day’s Night’, ‘Ticket To Ride’, and ‘I Am The Walrus’ had been released in America. The Capitol Records release also contained a unique edit of ‘I Should Have Known Better’ which fixed the harmonica drop-out during the introduction, which was unique to that pressing.

The Beatles’ Movie Medley

The US album was released on the same day as ‘The Beatles’ Movie Medley’, a 7″ single combining snippets of ‘Magical Mystery Tour’, ‘All You Need Is Love’, ‘You’ve Got To Hide Your Love Away’, ‘I Should Have Known Better’, ‘A Hard Day’s Night’, ‘Ticket To Ride’, and ‘Get Back’. It was edited by Capitol Records producer John Palladino.

In the UK, EMI/Parlophone initially chose not to release the medley, considering it lacking in quality. However, they changed course after demand for the US release led to imported copies.

The single was originally released with ‘Fab Four On Film’, an interview with the band about the making of the A Hard Day’s Night film, on the b-side. However, later copies had ‘I’m Happy To Dance With You’ instead.
